_comment: Auto-post + push copy per alert source. Loaded by AlertDispatchService at boot; editable without a redeploy. Placeholders: {mag}, {place} — and ONLY those two. An unresolved slot has its whole sentence dropped at dispatch and is logged + Sentry-captured (audit P0-5, where a literal "{distance}mi {direction}" reached an APNs push). {distance}/{direction} are gone for good: distance is per-recipient and the push is one batched multicast for up to 500 people, so it cannot be personalised without abandoning the batch. {name} is gone because it resolved to the word "Warning". Spec: docs/ALERTS_INTEGRATION.md. Copy target is 6th-8th grade reading level — action first, no acronyms, no meteorological jargon. Measured against the live feed in AlertTemplateCoverageTest.
_matching: NWS templates match on `eventAny` — the EXACT product name from api.weather.gov/alerts/types (111 values). This replaced substring-matching the headline (audit P0-2), which matched only 26 of 310 live alerts and gave 19% of those the wrong copy: 'Flood' is a substring of 'Flood Watch', so watches dispatched as warnings. Exact names also mean a future NWS rename fails the coverage test instead of silently disabling a hazard — which is exactly what happened when 'Excessive Heat Warning' became 'Extreme Heat Warning' and heat alerts went dark.
_tiers: `tier` is warning | watch. Only `warning` earns a push (AlertDispatchService.isLifeThreatening); a watch gets a feed post and nothing that interrupts. This is the structural version of the Watch/Warning distinction that previously lived only inside a raw title string. Advisories are deliberately absent: they are Attention-mode per ALERTS_INTEGRATION.md, and giving them a template would put them in the push path.
templates: --- NWS · WARNING tier · take action now ---

templates.headline: Tornado warning
templates.body: Tornado spotted. Get to the lowest floor and an inside room with no windows — right now.

templates.headline: Severe thunderstorm warning
templates.body: Damaging wind and hail are moving in. Go inside now, stay off the road, and keep away from windows.

templates.headline: Flash flood warning
templates.body: Flash flood happening now. Turn around, don't drown. Get to higher ground.

templates.headline: Flood warning
templates.body: Flooding is happening. Move what you can upstairs. Never drive through water — turn around, don't drown.

templates.headline: Hurricane warning
templates.body: A hurricane is on the way. Bring loose things inside, fill up on water, charge your phones, and look at your evacuation plan now.

templates.headline: Tropical storm warning
templates.body: Strong winds and heavy rain are coming. Bring loose things inside, charge your phones, and fill up on water.

templates.headline: Blizzard warning
templates.body: Stay off the roads. Have food, water, and a backup way to stay warm. Check on neighbors who live alone.

templates.headline: Winter storm warning
templates.body: Heavy snow or ice is coming. Get water, food, and a way to stay warm. Power may go out — check on neighbors who live alone.

templates.headline: Dangerous cold
templates.body: Cold this bad can hurt you in minutes. Stay inside, cover every bit of skin if you go out, and check on older neighbors.

templates.headline: Dangerous heat
templates.body: Heat this high can make you sick fast. Drink water, find air conditioning, and skip outdoor work. Check on older neighbors and anyone without AC.

templates.headline: Fire danger is high
templates.body: Any fire that starts today will spread fast. Don't burn anything outside. Pack a small bag in case you have to leave quickly.

templates.headline: Fire warning
templates.body: A fire is burning near you. Get your go-bag, keep your phone on, and be ready to leave the moment you're told to.

templates.headline: High wind warning
templates.body: Strong winds can bring down trees and power lines. Bring loose things inside and stay away from downed lines.

templates.headline: Dust storm warning
templates.body: You may not be able to see the road. If you're driving, pull all the way off, turn your lights off, and keep your foot off the brake.

templates.headline: Avalanche warning
templates.body: Stay off and out from under steep slopes. Don't travel in the backcountry today.

templates.headline: Tsunami warning
templates.body: Leave the beach and low ground now. Get high up or far inland on foot if you can. Don't wait to see the water.

templates.headline: Volcano warning
templates.body: Follow what local officials tell you. Stay inside, close windows and vents, and wear a mask if there's ash in the air.

templates.headline: Earthquake warning
templates.body: Drop, cover, and hold on. Stay away from windows. Expect more shaking after the first.

templates.headline: Unhealthy air
templates.body: Stay inside and keep windows shut. Set your AC to recirculate. Wear an N95 if you have to go out.

templates: --- NWS · WARNING tier · civil / non-weather emergencies relayed through NWS ---

These are IPAWS-originated messages a local authority pushed through the NWS dissemination path. Coverage is inconsistent by jurisdiction, so their PRESENCE is not a guarantee and their ABSENCE is not an all-clear — but when one arrives it is the single most important thing on the screen. See the P0-6 note in the epic tracker.

templates.headline: Leave now
templates.body: Officials are telling people in your area to get out now. Take your go-bag, your medicines, and your people. Don't wait to pack more.

templates.headline: Stay where you are
templates.body: Go inside now and stay there. Shut all doors and windows, turn off fans and AC, and wait for officials to say it's safe.

templates.headline: Emergency in your area
templates.body: Officials have sent an emergency message for your area. Read it, do what it says, and stay off the phone unless you need help.

templates.headline: Chemical or radiation danger
templates.body: Go inside now. Shut doors, windows, and vents, and turn off anything pulling in outside air. Wait for officials to say it's safe.

templates: --- NWS · WATCH tier · get ready, do not interrupt ---

templates.headline: Tornado watch
templates.body: Tornadoes are possible today. Pick the room you'd go to — lowest floor, no windows — and keep your phone charged.

templates.headline: Severe thunderstorm watch
templates.body: Strong storms are possible today. Bring loose things inside and keep your phone charged.

templates.headline: Flood watch
templates.body: Flooding is possible. Move anything valuable up off the floor and plan a route that avoids low roads.

templates.headline: Hurricane watch
templates.body: A storm may reach you in about two days. Fill up on water and gas, refill medicines, and read your evacuation plan now.

templates.headline: Winter storm watch
templates.body: Heavy snow or ice is possible. Stock up on food and water, and get a backup way to stay warm before it starts.

templates.headline: Hard freeze coming
templates.body: Cover outdoor pipes and let faucets drip. Bring in pets and plants, and get warm layers ready.

templates.headline: Dangerous heat coming
templates.body: It's going to get dangerously hot. Find a cool place you can go, stock up on water, and plan to check on older neighbors.

templates.headline: Fire weather watch
templates.body: Conditions may turn dangerous for fire. Don't burn anything outside, and put a small go-bag by the door.

templates.headline: High wind watch
templates.body: Strong winds are possible. Bring loose things inside and expect the power may go out.

templates.headline: Avalanche watch
templates.body: Avalanche danger is rising. Put off backcountry trips and check conditions before you go anywhere near steep slopes.

templates.headline: Tsunami watch
templates.body: A tsunami may be coming. Stay off the beach, know your route to high ground, and keep your phone on.

templates.headline: Earthquake felt nearby
templates.body: Magnitude {mag} earthquake — {place}. Check your home for damage. Smell for gas and look for water leaks.

templates: --- FEMA · recovery context, never a push ---

templates.headline: FEMA disaster declared
templates.body: FEMA declared a disaster in your area. You may be able to get help with housing, repairs, or other costs — fema.gov/assistance

templates.headline: FEMA wildfire disaster declared
templates.body: FEMA declared a wildfire disaster in your area. You may be able to get help with housing, repairs, or other costs — fema.gov/assistance

templates.headline: FEMA disaster declared
templates.body: FEMA declared a disaster in your area. You may be able to get help with housing, repairs, or other costs — fema.gov/assistance
